{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/trial.csv')

# Check for sentinel values in biomarker_baseline
sentinel_count = (df['biomarker_baseline'] == -999).sum()
print(f'Number of -999 sentinel values in biomarker_baseline: {sentinel_count}')

# Check for duplicates in patient_id
patient_id_counts = df['patient_id'].value_counts()
duplicate_patients = patient_id_counts[patient_id_counts > 1]
print(f'Number of patients with multiple rows: {len(duplicate_patients)}')

# Show the sample_seq distribution per patient to confirm re-testing
sample_seq_max = df.groupby('patient_id')['sample_seq'].max()
print(f'Number of patients with sample_seq > 1: {len(sample_seq_max[sample_seq_max > 1])}')

# Note: The data dictionary says to keep only the highest sample_seq per patient
# So we deduplicate accordingly

# First, filter out rows where biomarker_baseline is -999
filtered_df = df[df['biomarker_baseline'] != -999]

# Then deduplicate on patient_id, keeping the highest sample_seq
deduped_df = filtered_df.loc[filtered_df.groupby('patient_id')['sample_seq'].idxmax()]

# Now compute the mean baseline biomarker value
mean_baseline = deduped_df['biomarker_baseline'].mean()

print(f'Mean baseline biomarker value (ng/mL) across all patients: {mean_baseline}')"}
